facts.statement: Neopetalichthys yenmenpaensis was an extinct placoderm that lived in China during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Neopetalichthys yenmenpaensis is an extinct petalichthid placoderm from the Early Devonian of China.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Neopetalichthys is a poorly preserved partial skull found in Emsian-aged rock layers in Sichuan.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen is a poorly preserved partial, and elongated skull from Emsian-aged strata in Sichuan.

facts.statement: The skull of Neopetalichthys may have been approximately 8.5 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull may be around 8.5 cm in length.

facts.statement: Some researchers have questioned whether Neopetalichthys belongs within the Petalichthyida, classifying it instead as a placoderm of uncertain placement.
facts.quote: Phylogeny Denison 1978 questions Neopetalichthys' placement within Petalichthyida, regarding it as Placodermi incertae sedis

facts.statement: A 1991 study confirmed Neopetalichthys as a petalichthyid but still regarded it as a basal form of uncertain placement.
facts.quote: According to Zhu's 1991 redescription of Diandongpetalichthys, Neopetalichthys' status as a petalichthyid is confirmed, though, in that study, it is regarded as a basal incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Neopetalichthys is possibly closely related to Quasipetalichthys, though their family grouping remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Quasipetalichthys is possibly closely related to Neopetalichthys, and may or may not be placed together within Quasipetalichthyidae.

facts.statement: Neopetalichthys is classified within the parent group Placodermi.
